parts.title: The green jacket
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When I was fourteen, I hated the idea of wearing clothes that had belonged to someone else. My cousin Kayode loved charity shops, and every time he visited, he tried to take me to one. I always found an excuse. I thought the clothes would smell strange and look old-fashioned, and I was worried that my friends would laugh at me.

One rainy Saturday, however, there was nothing else to do, so I finally agreed to go with him. The shop was bigger than I had expected, and it was quiet and warm. Kayode went straight to the back, but I stayed near the door, looking at a rack of coats. Then I saw a green jacket with a soft collar and brass buttons. It was in perfect condition, and it only cost eight pounds. I tried it on, and the sleeves fitted exactly.

I wore the jacket to school on Monday, and I was very nervous. To my surprise, three people asked me where I had bought it. One girl wanted to know if the shop had more like it. I felt proud, and I realised that nobody could tell the jacket was second-hand. Since then, I have found shirts, bags and even a pair of leather boots in charity shops. I still enjoy walking round them slowly and looking for something that nobody else has. Kayode says he knew I would change my mind, but he was too polite to say so at the time.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer avoid charity shops at first?
options: She thought the prices were too high.
She had never been inside a charity shop in her life.
She was afraid of what her friends would think.
She did not enjoy shopping with her cousin.
questions.explanation: She was worried that her friends would laugh at her, and she expected the clothes to look old-fashioned.

questions.prompt: What made her go to the shop on that Saturday?
options: There was nothing else to do.
She wanted to buy a coat.
She wanted to buy a present for him.
questions.explanation: It rained and there was nothing else to do, so she agreed to go.

questions.prompt: What did she like about the jacket?
options: It was a gift from her cousin.
Its colour matched her school uniform.
It was a present from the shop owner.
It was cheap and fitted her well.
questions.explanation: It cost only eight pounds and the sleeves fitted exactly.

questions.prompt: How did people react when she wore it to school?
options: They asked where she got it.
They wanted to borrow it for a party.
questions.explanation: Three people asked where she had bought it, and one girl wanted more shops like it.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say about Kayode at the end?
options: He now shops in different places.
He felt sorry about the idea.
He was right about her but did not say it.
He was angry that she had waited for so long.
questions.explanation: Kayode knew she would change her mind but was too polite to say so.

parts.title: A year without new clothes
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Last January, Mia from Kelby made a promise: she would not buy any new clothes for a whole year. She had noticed that her wardrobe was full, but she still felt that she had nothing to wear. [1] She hoped the challenge would show her how much she really needed.

The first few months were not easy. Whenever her friends went to the shopping centre, she felt left out. [2] Instead, she took a bag and went to the market to look for second-hand pieces, or she borrowed clothes from her older sister.

By summer, Mia was enjoying the challenge. She learned to sew on missing buttons and to turn old jeans into shorts. [3] People she did not know began to follow her, and many of them sent her their own ideas for mending clothes.

At the end of the year, Mia counted what she had saved. [4] She says that the biggest surprise was not the money but the way she felt. She no longer looked at adverts and thought she needed everything.

Will she go back to her old habits? [5] "I want to buy fewer things and keep them for longer," she says.
sentences: She did not want to spend her money on things she would wear only once.
Her brother bought a new coat and a pair of shoes last week.
So she decided to try something different.
She also started to write about her projects online.
Mia is sure that she will not.
A few of her friends also began to buy second-hand things.
It was more than four hundred pounds.
The shopping centre in Kelby is the biggest in the county.

gaps.explanation: "So she decided to try something different" follows her problem of having a full wardrobe but nothing to wear.
"Instead" follows the sentence about not buying at the shopping centre; sentence D explains why she avoided shops.
She learned to sew and mend, and then began to write about her projects online; the next sentences say that people followed her.
"It was more than four hundred pounds" answers what she counted, and the next sentence continues with the money.
The question "Will she go back to her old habits?" is answered by "Mia is sure that she will not."

parts.title: Dressing for the weather
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Choosing the right clothes can make a big [1] to how you feel on a cold day. Experts say that it is better to wear several thin layers [2] one thick coat, because you can take a layer off if you get too warm. Wool and cotton are good [3] for the bottom layer, as they keep your skin dry. Do not forget your hands and head: you lose a lot of heat [4] them. When it rains, a coat with a hood is more useful than an umbrella, especially if it is windy, [5] an umbrella is difficult to hold. Finally, it is worth spending a little more on warm socks, because cold feet can quickly [6] you unhappy.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: You say that something "makes a difference" to how you feel.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: "Instead of" means one choice replaces the other: thin layers instead of one thick coat.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: "Good choices" means good things to choose; the other words do not fit with "for the bottom layer".

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: Heat escapes "through" the head and hands.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: "Because" gives the reason why an umbrella is difficult to hold when it is windy.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: The structure is "make someone + adjective": make you unhappy.

parts.title: A message about shopping
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Dear Tom,
I am writing to tell you about my shopping trip. I went to the new shopping centre [1] Saturday with my sister. We spent most [2] the afternoon looking for a dress for her birthday party, and in the end she chose the first one [3] had tried on! The shop was very busy, so we had to wait [4] a long time to pay. I also bought a pair of boots [5] I really love, but they cost more than I had planned. In future, I am going [6] buy my clothes at the market.
Lia

gaps.explanation: We use "on" with a day of the week: on Saturday.
"Most of the afternoon" is the fixed pattern: most of + noun phrase.
The relative clause needs a subject: the first one she had tried on.
We say "wait for a long time" for the length of the wait.
A relative pronoun links "boots" with the clause: boots that I really love.
The structure for plans is "be going to" + base verb.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: odalys
turns.text: Excuse me. I like this shirt for my brother’s birthday. Have you got it in blue?

turns.speaker: teodor
turns.text: Yes, we have it in blue, in small and large. Which size does he wear?

turns.speaker: odalys
turns.text: Hmm. Last year I bought him a large blue one and it was far too big. I nearly picked the small one just now, but he’s grown since then.

turns.speaker: teodor
turns.text: Then try the medium. We have it in green and it’s selling quickly.

turns.speaker: odalys
turns.text: Green is his favourite colour, actually. The medium one in green, please.

turns.speaker: teodor
turns.text: Lovely. Shall I put it in a bag?

turns.speaker: odalys
turns.text: Please, and I’ll pay at the till.

question.prompt: What does the woman decide to buy?
question.explanation: Last year’s large blue shirt was too big and she nearly took the small one, but he has grown and green is his favourite colour, so she buys the medium green one.

turns.speaker: wendell
turns.text: Look at all these scarves. Do you like the red one? It’s very bright.

turns.speaker: perpetua
turns.text: It’s nice, but I wore red last winter. What about the striped one? It’s on sale.

turns.speaker: wendell
turns.text: The stripes are a bit loud for my dad, and it’s a present. He only wears dark colours.

turns.speaker: perpetua
turns.text: You’re right. His coat is grey, and it matches everything he owns, so let’s get one in that colour. It’s softer, too.

turns.speaker: wendell
turns.text: Good thinking. I’ll ask the assistant for a box.

turns.speaker: perpetua
turns.text: And I’ll find a card.

question.explanation: Red is too bright and she wore it last winter, and the stripes are too loud for a man who wears dark colours, so they choose the soft grey one.

turns.speaker: ximena
turns.text: Good afternoon. Can I help you?

turns.speaker: rafferty
turns.text: Yes, I’d like this jacket. The label says fifty pounds. Is that right?

turns.speaker: ximena
turns.text: That’s the normal price, but this week we have a small discount. With your student card, I can take two pounds off.

turns.speaker: rafferty
turns.text: Excellent, I have it here. A friend of mine bought a similar jacket for forty pounds at the market, but the quality wasn’t good.

turns.speaker: ximena
turns.text: Ours is better. So the total is your price after the reduction. Card or cash?

turns.speaker: rafferty
turns.text: Card, please.

question.prompt: How much will the man pay?
question.explanation: The label price is fifty pounds, the market jacket cost forty, and the student discount takes two pounds off the price, so he pays forty-eight.

turns.speaker: beryl
turns.text: Hello, this is Beryl, and I’m calling about the dress that I bought online on Monday. I want to return it. At first I thought there was a hole near the sleeve, but it was just a shadow in the photo. The colour is exactly the one on the website, and I like the pattern. The real problem is that I tried it on this morning and I can’t breathe. It’s too tight around the waist. Please tell me how to send it back. Thank you very much, goodbye.

question.prompt: What is wrong with the dress?
options: There is a hole in it.
question.explanation: She says the hole was only a shadow and the colour is the same as the website, but the dress is too tight around the waist.

turns.speaker: cosmo
turns.text: Hi Yvette, it’s Cosmo. I’m phoning about your walk in the mountains on Sunday. I know you want to buy new boots today, but the shops close at one and you need time to break them in, so don’t do it. Your old ones are fine. Light sandals sound comfortable, but the rocks are sharp near the top, so please leave them at home. The most useful thing is an extra pair of socks in your bag. When your feet get wet, you’ll be glad to change them. Have a great time, and send me a photo!

question.prompt: What does the man advise the woman to do?
options: Buy a new pair of boots today
Wear a pair of light sandals
question.explanation: New boots would not be broken in and sandals are not safe on sharp rocks, so the useful advice is to carry an extra pair of socks.

turns.speaker: maribel
turns.text: Anselm, did you find everything for the trip? You always forget something.

turns.speaker: anselm
turns.text: I’m not sure. Daisy lost her hat last winter, and I don’t want that to happen again. This time it’s in her bag with her scarf. But I can only find the left glove.

turns.speaker: maribel
turns.text: The right one is probably under the sofa. Daisy leaves her things everywhere.

turns.speaker: anselm
turns.text: I’ve looked there already. It’s gone. I’ll buy a new pair tomorrow before we leave.

turns.speaker: maribel
turns.text: Good idea. It’s freezing up there.

question.explanation: The hat was lost last winter and the scarf is in her bag, but Anselm can find only one of the pair of gloves, so she has lost a glove.

turns.speaker: lorcan
turns.text: Hi Thea, it’s Lorcan. About tonight. I said we’d meet at the bus stop near the station, but my bus is always late on Fridays, so forget that. The film starts at eight at the cinema on the corner, but it’s very cold, and I don’t want you to wait there on your own. So let’s meet outside the clothes shop, the one where we bought your yellow jacket. It’s got a big window, so you can stay warm and look at the dresses. See you at half past seven!

options: At the bus stop near the station
At the cinema on the corner
question.explanation: The bus stop is rejected because the bus is late and the cinema is too cold to wait outside, so they will meet at the shop where they bought her jacket.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: portia
turns.text: Jarvis, why are you looking so sad? You were so excited about the party tonight.

turns.speaker: jarvis
turns.text: I wanted to wear my new jeans, but I tried them on and they don’t close. I only got them in September.

turns.speaker: portia
turns.text: Did Mum buy the wrong ones?

turns.speaker: jarvis
turns.text: No, they were the right size then. I just grew about five centimetres this year. I looked everywhere for my old trousers, but I can’t find those either.

turns.speaker: portia
turns.text: That’s not a disaster. We can go to the shop after lunch.

turns.speaker: jarvis
turns.text: But I wanted to feel good about these ones.

options: His jeans are too small now.
His mother bought the wrong size.
question.explanation: The size was right in September and he found nothing else; what upsets him is that he has grown and the jeans do not close.

turns.speaker: marlowe
turns.text: Good morning, Style Direct. How can I help you?

turns.speaker: serena
turns.text: Hi. I ordered a coat two weeks ago and it still hasn’t arrived. I’m sick of waiting for the delivery. The website shows a green light and the word on its way.

turns.speaker: marlowe
turns.text: Let me check. Do you want to cancel it or change the size?

turns.speaker: serena
turns.text: No, the order is fine. I made it on the website without any trouble. I just need the coat before my trip on Friday.

turns.speaker: marlowe
turns.text: I see it here. The courier says tomorrow morning.

turns.speaker: serena
turns.text: Great. Please send me a message when it leaves the depot.

options: She is waiting for a delivery.
She wants to change her order.
question.explanation: She can use the website and does not want to change the order; she is calling because the coat has not arrived and she needs it by Friday.

turns.speaker: delphine
turns.text: Have you seen the new school uniform, Nikolai? They put the picture on the website.

turns.speaker: nikolai
turns.text: I have. It’s dark blue with a white shirt. A bit boring, I think.

turns.speaker: delphine
turns.text: Actually, I like it. The old grey one made everybody look tired, and this has lighter material for summer. And look at the price, it costs less than the old one.

turns.speaker: nikolai
turns.text: You’re right. I tried the trousers on, and they’re soft.

turns.speaker: delphine
turns.text: See? A big improvement. I can’t wait to wear it.

turns.speaker: nikolai
turns.text: Well, I’m not so sure about the tie.

question.prompt: What does the girl think of the new uniform?
question.explanation: She says the old grey one looked tired, the new material is lighter and the price is lower, so she believes it is better than the old uniform.

turns.speaker: osbert
turns.text: Inge, do you think this suit is too much for the party? Everyone will be in jeans.

turns.speaker: inge
turns.text: It’s very smart. Maybe a bit formal, a bit serious.

turns.speaker: osbert
turns.text: That’s what I think! And my tie is so dark. I’ll look as if I’m going to a funeral.

turns.speaker: inge
turns.text: Don’t panic. Take off the tie and open the shirt a little. We can go in ten minutes. The taxi is booked and it’s quite cheap.

turns.speaker: osbert
turns.text: I’m not worried about the money or the time. I just don’t want to stand out.

turns.speaker: inge
turns.text: You’ll be fine, trust me.

question.prompt: What is the man worried about?
question.explanation: He is not worried about the money or the time; he fears that his suit and dark tie are too serious for a party where people wear jeans.

turns.speaker: tamsin2
turns.text: Barnaby, is that my red shirt that you’re wearing?

turns.speaker: barnaby
turns.text: Er, yes. I needed something smart for the interview, and mine were in the wash.

turns.speaker: tamsin2
turns.text: You could have asked me! I found the drawer empty this morning.

turns.speaker: barnaby
turns.text: Sorry, I really am. I’ll wash it tonight, and I promise there isn’t a mark on it.

turns.speaker: tamsin2
turns.text: I’m not angry about the shirt. I’d have said yes. I just hate it when you take my things behind my back.

turns.speaker: barnaby
turns.text: You’re right. Next time I’ll ask first.

options: He damaged one of her favourite shirts.
He took her shirt without asking.
He lost her new red shirt yesterday.
question.explanation: He has not damaged or lost the shirt and she would have agreed; she is annoyed because he borrowed it without asking her.

turns.speaker: gregor
turns.text: Hattie, do you sew? I need to change this jacket.

turns.speaker: hattie
turns.text: What’s wrong with it? It looks fine to me. The sleeve isn’t torn.

turns.speaker: gregor
turns.text: No, it isn’t. And I love the size, I wouldn’t want a different one. The problem is that my arms are not so long, so the cuffs cover my hands.

turns.speaker: hattie
turns.text: I see. We can take it up by three centimetres at the end of each arm. It’s an easy job.

turns.speaker: gregor
turns.text: Perfect. How much would it be?

turns.speaker: hattie
turns.text: Ten pounds. Come back on Thursday.

options: A new jacket in a smaller size
A repair to a broken sleeve
question.explanation: The jacket is not torn and the size is right, but the sleeves are too long and cover his hands, so he wants them shortened.

parts.title: A talk about a school fashion show
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Good morning, everyone. I’m Bronwyn, and I’m in charge of this year’s fashion show at Rowan School. First, the day. The show takes place on Friday evening. We wanted Saturday, but the building is used for a wedding, so Friday it is. The doors open at half past six, and the show starts at seven o’clock. Please be on time, because the first models walk out at five past. Now, the clothes. Last year the students bought cheap cotton in the market, but this time everything has to be made of recycled materials. We are using old curtains, plastic bags and even bicycle tyres. Some of the results are surprising. One girl made a lovely evening dress from newspapers! Where will it be? Many people think we’ll use the gym, because we did last time, but the floor was too hard and noisy. We’ll be in the school hall, with a proper stage and lights. A friend of the school is lending us a long walkway for the models. Now, tickets. Adults pay six pounds in the normal way, but for students and for pensioners it is only four pounds, and that is the price you pay if you buy in advance. Children under seven come in free. The seats are numbered, so the early buyers get the best ones. You can buy tickets in the office before the show, or from me after class. Finally, what is the money for? Some of you suggested a new minibus, and the music teacher hopes for a drum kit, but we decided to buy a piano for the hall, because the old one is broken and can’t be repaired. Please tell your friends and your families, and bring a warm coat, because the hall can be cold in the evening. Thank you for listening, and I hope to see you all there on Friday.

gaps.prompt: The show takes place on a ___ evening
gaps.explanation: The show is on Friday evening because Saturday is taken by a wedding.

gaps.prompt: The show begins at ___ in the evening
gaps.explanation: The doors open at half past six and the show starts at seven o’clock.

gaps.prompt: All the clothes must be made of ___ materials
gaps.explanation: Last year they used cheap cotton; this year everything is recycled.

gaps.prompt: The event will be held in the school ___
gaps.explanation: Not the gym but the school hall, with a stage.

gaps.prompt: Students and pensioners pay ___ pounds for a ticket
gaps.explanation: Adults pay six pounds; students and pensioners pay four pounds.

gaps.prompt: The money raised will be spent on a ___ for the hall
gaps.explanation: A minibus and a drum kit were suggested, but they will buy a piano.

parts.title: An interview with a costume maker
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Ottoline, you make costumes for the theatre. How did your career begin?

turns.speaker: ottoline
turns.text: Well, I dreamed of going to the famous drama school in London, but I didn’t get a place, so that’s not it. And I did help my mother sometimes in her little shop, though only at weekends. What really started it was my teacher at school. She saw me sewing a bag for a friend during break, and she asked if I’d like to do the costumes for the end-of-year play.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What do you do first with a new play?

turns.speaker: ottoline
turns.text: I read the script several times, and I’m trying to understand each character. Are they shy, angry, rich? The colours and the shapes come later. I do meet the actors, of course, but not at the start, because they sometimes have strong opinions that confuse me. First I need to know who these people are.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Why do you often use old clothes?

turns.speaker: ottoline
turns.text: Lots of people expect me to say that it’s for the planet, and that’s a nice bonus, but it isn’t my main reason. Nor do I think they look better. New cloth is often prettier! The truth is that theatres have very small budgets. A shop dress would eat my whole month’s money, so I look in charity shops and my friends’ wardrobes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What is the hardest part of the job?

turns.speaker: ottoline
turns.text: Actors are lovely, so I don’t find talking to them hard. And repairing big costumes is slow, but it’s relaxing. The hard thing is the deadline. Sometimes a director changes the idea three days before the opening night, and I have to make ten costumes in a weekend. I work through the night, and I’m exhausted.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: You listen to the actors’ complaints. Why?

turns.speaker: ottoline
turns.text: A few of them do have clever ideas, for example moving a pocket, but I don’t do it for that. And I’m not trying to keep them happy either. I listen because the audience can see when someone is uncomfortable. If a collar scratches, the actor moves strangely, and people in the third row notice it.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What advice do you give young people?

turns.speaker: ottoline
turns.text: Read history, if you like, but history books won’t solve everything. Working in a shop is useful too, though you can learn that later. My best tip is to sit in a café and watch people dress. See how they walk in their clothes, which colours they choose, what they hide. That’s where every character comes from.

questions.prompt: How did Ottoline begin her career in costumes?
options: She trained at a famous school.
questions.explanation: She did not get into the famous school and only helped her mother at weekends; a teacher saw her sewing a bag and asked her to do the play.

questions.prompt: What does she do first with a new play?
options: Choose the colours of the cloth.
Talk to the actors about their ideas.
questions.explanation: She reads the script to understand each character and meets the actors and chooses colours later.

questions.prompt: Why does she often use old clothes?
options: She prefers the way they look.
Theatres do not have much money.
It is better for the environment.
questions.explanation: The planet is only a bonus and she thinks new cloth is prettier; the real reason is that theatres have small budgets.

questions.prompt: What does she find most difficult?
questions.explanation: She finds talking to actors easy and repairs relaxing; the hard thing is the deadline when a director changes the idea.

questions.prompt: Why does she listen to actors' complaints?
options: They sometimes have useful ideas about the design.
She wants the actors to stay happy with her.
The audience can see their discomfort.
questions.explanation: Clever ideas and keeping them happy are not her reason; she listens because the audience can see when someone is uncomfortable.

questions.prompt: What does she tell young people to do?
questions.explanation: History and shop work are less important; the best tip is to sit in a café and watch how people dress.
